surface: persisted-state claims + authority-side admission/writers (scope AUTHORITY seam)

findings.title: Forged element-root claim on a save with no committed element is admitted and permanently bricks the Ngu Hanh initiation
findings.description: PHAP_TU_ELEMENT_ROOT_IDS nodes (hoa_linh_ngo etc.) have exactly one writer: commitFiveElementInitiation, which commits the element root atomically with cultivationPath/cultivationWay, spellPath.element, the qi_refining realm advance and the element kit basic. The nodeLevels replay in saveShapeValidation.ts only replays the node's authored prereqs (node/excludesNode/nodeCount/realm); it never cross-checks an owned root against player.spellPath.element, and nothing restricts a mortal save's nodeLevels to core_* grants. A crafted mortal save claiming 'hoa_linh_ngo' (element=null) passes validateGameSaveShape AND assertSaveAcceptable. At commitFiveElementInitiation every element's purchasability probe then fails: the claimed element's root fails the owned check (getNodeLevel>0) and the other four fail excludesNode, so 'element_root_blocked' is returned for all five elements forever. The accepted save loads a permanently bricked progression state no writer can produce.
findings.repro: game/tests/architecture/a19ElementRootWitness.qa.test.ts > 'a mortal save claiming an element root bricks every initiation probe' -- shape.ok === true (defect), all 5 canPurchaseNode probes return false (brick evidence). npx vitest run tests/architecture/a19ElementRootWitness.qa.test.ts.
findings.mintPath: saveShapeValidation nodeLevels prereq replay (game/src/services/save/saveShapeValidation.ts ~1680) admits the root -> restore -> GameManagerRealmAdvanceOps.commitFiveElementInitiation element_root_blocked for every element (game/src/core/game/GameManagerRealmAdvanceOps.ts ~631-638) -> mortal player permanently unable to initiate.
findings.confidence: Confirmed (deterministic failing-test repro on the pinned commit; brick verified through the same canPurchaseNode call the ritual uses)
findings.scopeNote: Not a counter/counter-within-bounds class: the claim is an unproducible cross-field witness (element root without the element the ritual grants with it), i.e. persisted authority outside every writer's envelope.

findings.surface: save boundary -> player.spellPath.element on committed saves
findings.title: A committed spell_pathway save carrying element=null is unproducible yet admitted
findings.description: The ONLY element commit is commitFiveElementInitiation, which is also the ONLY way onto spell_pathway (element-axis ways can never ride the generic chooseCultivationPath op). Every writer-produced spell_pathway save therefore carries spellPath.element != null. The boundary accepts { element: null } on a committed save anyway: the element-axis ownership check gates writes to the axis but does not require the axis to be filled, and the NOVA-5 acceptance coherence check only fires when an element is resolved. The resulting player mints way authority (spell MP pool modifiers, five_elements_art holder, starter kit) with no element and can never gain one (selectSpellPathElement refuses realmId != 'mortal'), leaving the elemental_casting capability and the element tree dead. Unproducible persisted state admitted; effect is weaker than A19-1 because the player is not bricked from an already-valid position - they simply play a reduced, unreachable-by-writers progression shape.
findings.repro: Same file, test 'a committed spell_pathway save with element = null is unproducible' -- shape.ok === true, isSaveAcceptable === true (defect).
findings.mintPath: validateSpellPathPersistedState ownership check (game/src/core/phap-tu/PhapTuPath.ts) + saveAcceptance element->kit coherence (game/src/services/save/saveAcceptance.ts) both pass on element=null -> restore mints spell way authority (collectActiveWayStatModifiers + technique holder) with dead element machinery.
findings.confidence: Confirmed (deterministic failing-test repro; unproducibility established from the single-writer invariant in GameManagerRealmAdvanceOps + selectSpellPathElement's mortal-only gate)
findings.scopeNote: Same coherence-hole family as A19-1 (element axis lacks the commit-side witness replay). Kept separate because its admitted shape mints live way authority rather than a brick.
